1:1.t: Hacaliah: the KJV spells it Hachaliah. Kislev: the KJV's "Chisleu", the ninth month, November to December. "The twentieth year": of King Artaxerxes (2:1), 445 BC. "The citadel of Susa": the KJV's "Shushan the palace". Susa was a winter capital of the Persian kings.

1:2.t: "One of my brothers": Hanani may be Nehemiah's own brother (compare 7:2) or a fellow Jew.

"Remnant", "escaped" (Hebrew sheerit and peletah): sheerit is what is left over after a disaster, and peletah is those who escaped it. The prophets use these words for the people God keeps for Himself after judgment (Isaiah 10:20-22). See Ezra 9:8.

1:5.t: "Awesome": the KJV's "terrible", in the old sense of causing fear and awe.

"Covenant and steadfast love" (Hebrew berit and hesed): the KJV's "covenant and mercy". hesed is loyal, committed love that keeps its promises, especially within a covenant; no single English word covers it, and the KJV uses "mercy", "kindness" and "lovingkindness" (see Genesis 24:27 and Ezra 3:11). berit, "covenant", is a binding agreement that sets up a relationship with promises and obligations on both sides. Together the words mean that God keeps His promises out of loyal love, not only out of duty.

1:8.t: Nehemiah sums up Moses' words rather than quoting one passage; compare Leviticus 26:33 and Deuteronomy 30:1-5.

1:9.t: "The farthest edge of the sky": the KJV's "the uttermost part of the heaven", meaning the ends of the earth under the sky.

"Return" (Hebrew shuv): the basic Old Testament word for repentance. It means to turn around and go back, a change of direction more than a feeling. God's promise answers it: if they "return" to Him, He will bring them back (the same idea) to the land.

1:11.t: "Cupbearer": the officer who served the king's wine and tasted it first; a post of high trust.

2:1.t: Nisan is the first month, March to April, four months after Kislev (1:1).

2:3.t: "The city where my ancestors are buried": the KJV's "the place of my fathers' sepulchres".

2:8.t: "The fortress next to the temple": the KJV's "the palace which appertained to the house". The Hebrew birah means a fortress or citadel.

2:10.t: "The Ammonite official": the KJV's "the servant, the Ammonite". "Servant" here is a title for a royal official. Sanballat was governor of Samaria. "Horonite" probably means he came from Beth-horon.

2:19.t: "The Ammonite official": the KJV's "the servant, the Ammonite". "Servant" here is a title for a royal official. Sanballat was governor of Samaria. "Horonite" probably means he came from Beth-horon.

2:13.t: "Dragon Spring": as in the KJV. The Hebrew tannin can also mean a serpent or a jackal. "Dung Gate": the KJV's "dung port", the gate through which refuse was carried out.

3:1.t: "Tower of the Hundred": the KJV's "tower of Meah"; meah is the Hebrew word for "hundred". Hananel: the KJV spells it Hananeel.
The repairs are listed going around the wall counterclockwise, starting and ending at the Sheep Gate north of the temple.

3:4.t: Uriah and Hakkoz: the KJV spells them Urijah and Koz. Meshezabel: the KJV spells it Meshezabeel.

3:21.t: Uriah and Hakkoz: the KJV spells them Urijah and Koz. Meshezabel: the KJV spells it Meshezabeel.

3:5.t: "The men of Tekoa": the KJV's "the Tekoites". "Their Lord": as in the KJV. The Hebrew is plural, "their lords", and could mean God or the officials in charge of the work.

3:27.t: "The men of Tekoa": the KJV's "the Tekoites". "Their Lord": as in the KJV. The Hebrew is plural, "their lords", and could mean God or the officials in charge of the work.

3:6.t: Joiada: the KJV spells it Jehoiada here.

3:8.t: "One of the perfume makers": the KJV's "the son of one of the apothecaries". The Hebrew "son of" here means a member of the guild. "Restored": the KJV's "fortified". The Hebrew can also mean "left", that is, they left that stretch as it was.

3:9.t: and following "District": the KJV's "part" or "half part", a district of the province.

3:12.t: and following "District": the KJV's "part" or "half part", a district of the province.

3:10.t: Hashabneiah: the KJV spells it Hashabniah. 3:11, 3:23 Hasshub: the KJV spells it Hashub. 3:12 Hallohesh: the KJV spells it Halohesh. 3:14 Beth-haccherem: the KJV spells it Beth-haccerem. 3:18 Bavvai: the KJV spells it Bavai.

3:11.t: "Tower of the Ovens": the KJV's "tower of the furnaces", probably bakers' ovens.

3:13.t: KJV: "a thousand cubits on the wall".

3:14.t: Malchijah: the KJV spells it Malchiah.

3:31.t: Malchijah: the KJV spells it Malchiah.

"Inspection Gate": the KJV keeps the Hebrew name, "the gate Miphkad", meaning muster or inspection. "The ascent at the corner": the KJV's "the going up of the corner"; the Hebrew may mean an upper room.

3:15.t: "Pool of Siloam": the KJV's "pool of Siloah"; the Hebrew is Shelah.

3:16.t: "The House of the Mighty Men": the KJV's "the house of the mighty", perhaps a barracks for David's warriors.

3:22.t: "The men of the surrounding area": the KJV's "the men of the plain", probably the region around Jerusalem or the Jordan valley.

3:25.t: "Court of the guard": the KJV's "court of the prison".

3:26.t: "Ophel": a hill south of the temple. The KJV says the temple servants "dwelt in Ophel"; the sense is that they made repairs there.

4:1.t: In the Hebrew Bible these verses are numbered 3:33-38 and 4:1-17.

4:2.t: "Bring the stones back to life": the KJV's "revive the stones out of the heaps of the rubbish". Limestone that has been burned crumbles, so the stones were thought useless.

4:4.t: Nehemiah breaks off his account to pray, as he does often in this book (5:19, 6:9, 6:14, 13:14, 13:22, 13:29, 13:31).

4:7.t: "The people of Ashdod": the KJV's "the Ashdodites". With Samaria to the north, the Ammonites to the east, the Arabs to the south and Ashdod to the west, Jerusalem was surrounded.

4:12.t: "Whatever place you come back to us from, they will be upon you": as in the KJV. The Hebrew is hard; it may also mean "You must come back to us from every place where they live", a call to bring the workers home.

4:16.t: "Body armor": the KJV's "habergeons", coats of mail.

4:23.t: "Except that each one took them off to wash": as in the KJV. The Hebrew is very short, literally "each his weapon, the water", and many modern Bibles read that each kept his weapon in hand, even when going for water.

5:7.t: "Charging interest": the KJV's "exact usury". The law forbade charging interest to a fellow Israelite in need (Exodus 22:25, Leviticus 25:35-37).

5:11.t: "The hundredth part": one percent, probably a monthly rate of interest.

5:13.t: "The fold of my robe": the KJV's "my lap", the fold of a garment used as a pocket. Shaking it out was an acted curse.

5:14.t: "Food allowance of the governor": the KJV's "the bread of the governor", the food tax the governor had the right to collect. The twentieth to the thirty-second year of Artaxerxes is 445 to 433 BC.

5:15.t: KJV: "forty shekels of silver". The Hebrew may mean forty shekels a day.

6:2.t: Ono was a town near the coast, about 40 kilometers from Jerusalem.

6:5.t: "An open letter": an unsealed letter, meant to be read by others along the way.

6:6.t: Geshem: the KJV gives his name here in another form, Gashmu.

6:10.t: "Shut in at home": the KJV's "shut up". The Hebrew does not say why; he may have been acting out his warning, or kept away by ritual uncleanness. Mehetabel: the KJV spells it Mehetabeel.

6:11.t: Nehemiah was not a priest, so entering the temple building would have been a sin (Numbers 18:7).

6:15.t: Elul is the sixth month, August to September.

6:16.t: "They lost their confidence": the KJV's "they were much cast down in their own eyes".

6:18.t: "Bound to him by oath": the KJV's "sworn unto him", tied to him by marriage and agreements.

7:2.t: "The commander of the fortress": the KJV's "the ruler of the palace". The Hebrew birah means a fortress or citadel; see 2:8.

7:3.t: "Until the sun is hot": not at dawn, but well into the morning. "While the guards are still on duty": the KJV's "while they stand by".

7:6.t: This list repeats Ezra 2:1-70, with some differences in names and numbers, mostly from copying over the years. The "temple servants" (KJV "Nethinims", Hebrew "those given") were people given to serve in the temple; the "gatekeepers" (KJV "porters") were Levites who guarded the temple gates; the "governor" (KJV "Tirshatha") is a Persian title of honor. See the notes on Ezra 2.

7:28.t: Modern spellings: Kiriath-jearim, Michmash, Bethel, Pashhur, Tel-harsha, Hakkoz. The KJV spells them Kirjath-jearim, Michmas, Beth-el, Pashur, Tel-haresha, Koz. 7:46-55 Hasupha, Paseah, Nephushesim, Temah: the KJV spells them Hashupha, Phaseah, Nephishesim, Tamah.

7:41.t: Modern spellings: Kiriath-jearim, Michmash, Bethel, Pashhur, Tel-harsha, Hakkoz. The KJV spells them Kirjath-jearim, Michmas, Beth-el, Pashur, Tel-haresha, Koz. 7:46-55 Hasupha, Paseah, Nephushesim, Temah: the KJV spells them Hashupha, Phaseah, Nephishesim, Tamah.

7:61.t: Modern spellings: Kiriath-jearim, Michmash, Bethel, Pashhur, Tel-harsha, Hakkoz. The KJV spells them Kirjath-jearim, Michmas, Beth-el, Pashur, Tel-haresha, Koz. 7:46-55 Hasupha, Paseah, Nephushesim, Temah: the KJV spells them Hashupha, Phaseah, Nephishesim, Tamah.

7:63.t: Modern spellings: Kiriath-jearim, Michmash, Bethel, Pashhur, Tel-harsha, Hakkoz. The KJV spells them Kirjath-jearim, Michmas, Beth-el, Pashur, Tel-haresha, Koz. 7:46-55 Hasupha, Paseah, Nephushesim, Temah: the KJV spells them Hashupha, Phaseah, Nephishesim, Tamah.

7:70.t: KJV: "a thousand drams of gold", "twenty thousand drams of gold, and two thousand and two hundred pound of silver", "twenty thousand drams of gold, and two thousand pound of silver". The dram is the gold daric, a Persian coin of about 8.4 grams of gold, and the pound the mina, about 570 grams; see Ezra 2:69.

7:73.t: In many modern Bibles the second half of this verse begins chapter 8.

8:1.t: "Square": the KJV's "street", an open public place by the gate.

8:3.t: "Square": the KJV's "street", an open public place by the gate.

8:16.t: "Square": the KJV's "street", an open public place by the gate.

8:2.t: The first day of the seventh month was the Feast of Trumpets (Leviticus 23:24).

8:4.t: "Platform": the KJV's "pulpit", a raised stand. Uriah, Malchijah, Hashbaddanah: the KJV spells them Urijah, Malchiah, Hashbadana.

8:7.t: Hodiah: the KJV spells it Hodijah.

8:8.t: "Explained the meaning": the KJV's "gave the sense". This may mean they translated the Hebrew into Aramaic, which many of the people now spoke, as well as explaining it.

"Clearly" (Hebrew meforash): the word may mean "distinctly", "section by section", or "with interpretation", that is, translated. Jewish tradition took it to mean the reading was rendered into Aramaic, the start of the practice of the Targums.

8:9.t: "The governor": the KJV's "the Tirshatha", a Persian title of honor for a governor; see Ezra 2:63.

8:10.t: "Rich food" and "sweet drinks": the KJV's "the fat" and "the sweet".

"The joy of the LORD is your strength" (Hebrew chedvat YHWH, "joy"; maoz, "stronghold"): maoz means a place of safety, a fortress, more than inner energy. The phrase can mean the joy that comes from the LORD or the joy found in the LORD; either way it is a refuge. It is a call to celebrate a holy day, not a general rule about feelings.

8:14.t: "Shelters": the KJV's "booths", the huts made of branches for the Feast of Shelters (Leviticus 23:39-43).

8:15.t: "Pine": as in the KJV. The Hebrew may mean wild olive. "Other leafy trees": the KJV's "thick trees".

8:17.t: Joshua: the KJV spells it Jeshua here. The point is not that the feast had never been kept (see Ezra 3:4) but that it had not been kept like this, by the whole people living in shelters.

8:18.t: "A solemn assembly": the eighth day that closed the feast (Leviticus 23:36).

9:1.t: "This month": the seventh month (8:2), two days after the Feast of Shelters ended.

9:2.t: "Those of Israelite descent": the KJV's "the seed of Israel".

9:3.t: "A quarter of the day": the KJV's "one fourth part of the day", about three hours.

9:4.t: "Stairs": the KJV's word; probably a raised platform for the Levites.

9:5.t: Hashabneiah, Hodiah: the KJV spells them Hashabniah, Hodijah. The quotation marks open here because the Levites call the people to praise and then lead the prayer that follows. The Greek Old Testament puts "And Ezra said" before verse 6, so some Bibles make the prayer Ezra's.

9:6.t: "The highest heavens": the KJV's "the heaven of heavens". "Host": the stars, and the angels who serve God.

9:16.t: "Became stubborn": the KJV's "hardened their necks", a picture of an ox that will not take the yoke; also in verses 17 and 29.

9:17.t: "Appointed a leader to go back": as in the KJV, following Numbers 14:4. Some Hebrew manuscripts read "in Egypt" for "in their rebellion".

"Gracious and merciful, slow to anger and rich in steadfast love": these words quote God's description of Himself in Exodus 34:6, the most quoted statement about God's character in the Old Testament (also 9:31). Gracious (hannun) means showing undeserved favor; merciful (rahum) is related to the word for womb, a tender compassion.

9:18.t: "A calf of cast metal": the KJV's "a molten calf" (Exodus 32:4). "Great outrages": the KJV's "great provocations", acts that insulted God.

9:20.t: "Spirit": capitalized as the Spirit of God.

9:30.t: "Spirit": capitalized as the Spirit of God.

9:22.t: "Every corner of it": the KJV's "didst divide them into corners". The Hebrew is unclear; it may mean God gave Israel the outlying lands too. "The land of the king of Heshbon" is another name for the land of Sihon, who was king of Heshbon.

9:27.t: "Rescuers": the KJV's "saviours", meaning the judges God raised up to deliver Israel.

9:29.t: "By which a person who keeps them will live": the KJV's "which if a man do, he shall live in them", quoting Leviticus 18:5 (compare Romans 10:5, Galatians 3:12).

9:38.t: In the Hebrew Bible this verse is 10:1, and chapter 10 is numbered one higher throughout.
"A firm agreement" (Hebrew amanah): not the usual word for covenant (berit), but a word from the root aman, "firm, reliable", from which "Amen" also comes. It is a written pledge made firm by seals.

10:1.t: Zedekiah: the KJV spells it Zidkijah. Hacaliah: the KJV spells it Hachaliah; see 1:1.

10:3.t: Pashhur, Hasshub, Hodiah: the KJV spells them Pashur, Hashub, Hodijah.

10:23.t: Pashhur, Hasshub, Hodiah: the KJV spells them Pashur, Hashub, Hodijah.

10:10.t: Pashhur, Hasshub, Hodiah: the KJV spells them Pashur, Hashub, Hodijah.

10:11.t: Mica, Zattu, Hezekiah, Meshezabel, Pilha: the KJV spells them Micha, Zatthu, Hizkijah, Meshezabeel, Pileha.

10:14.t: Mica, Zattu, Hezekiah, Meshezabel, Pilha: the KJV spells them Micha, Zatthu, Hizkijah, Meshezabeel, Pileha.
Many of these "leaders" are family names found in the list of Ezra 2 and Nehemiah 7; the head of each family signed for it.

10:17.t: Mica, Zattu, Hezekiah, Meshezabel, Pilha: the KJV spells them Micha, Zatthu, Hizkijah, Meshezabeel, Pileha.

10:21.t: Mica, Zattu, Hezekiah, Meshezabel, Pilha: the KJV spells them Micha, Zatthu, Hizkijah, Meshezabeel, Pileha.

10:24.t: Mica, Zattu, Hezekiah, Meshezabel, Pilha: the KJV spells them Micha, Zatthu, Hizkijah, Meshezabeel, Pileha.

10:29.t: "Bound themselves with a curse and an oath": they called down a curse on themselves if they broke the oath.

10:31.t: "Let the land rest": the KJV's "leave the seventh year" (Exodus 23:10-11). "Cancel every debt": the KJV's "the exaction of every debt" (Deuteronomy 15:1-2).

10:32.t: KJV: "the third part of a shekel". The law asked for half a shekel at a census (Exodus 30:13); this was a smaller yearly gift.

10:33.t: "Bread of the Presence": the KJV's "shewbread", the loaves kept before the LORD in the sanctuary. "Grain offering": the KJV's "meat offering".

10:34.t: "The wood offering": wood for the altar fire, which had to burn without going out (Leviticus 6:12-13). The law does not name this offering; it was a new arrangement.

10:37.t: "Storerooms": the KJV's "chambers", rooms in the temple courts for storing offerings. "Contributions": the KJV's "offerings", the Hebrew terumah, a portion set aside for God.

10:38.t: "A tenth of the tithes": the Levites gave a tenth of what they received to the priests (Numbers 18:26).

11:1.t: "One out of every ten": the KJV's "one of ten", a tithe of the people for the city.

11:3.t: Compare the similar list in 1 Chronicles 9:2-17.

11:4.t: Mahalalel: the KJV spells it Mahalaleel.

11:5.t: "The son of the Shilonite": the KJV's "the son of Shiloni", probably meaning a descendant of Shelah, Judah's son.

11:6.t: "Capable men", "mighty men of valor": the KJV's "valiant men" and "mighty men of valour". The Hebrew can mean warriors or simply men of standing.

11:14.t: "Capable men", "mighty men of valor": the KJV's "valiant men" and "mighty men of valour". The Hebrew can mean warriors or simply men of standing.
"The son of one of the great men": as in the KJV. The Hebrew Haggedolim may also be a name.

11:7.t: Jeshaiah: the KJV spells it Jesaiah. 11:9 Hassenuah: the KJV's "Senuah". 11:13 Amashsai, Azarel, Ahzai: the KJV spells them Amashai, Azareel, Ahasai. 11:21 Gishpa: the KJV spells it Gispa. 11:26 Beth-pelet: the KJV spells it Beth-phelet. 11:28 Meconah: the KJV spells it Mekonah. 11:29 Zorah: the KJV spells it Zareah.

11:9.t: "Second in command over the city": the KJV's "second over the city". The Hebrew can also mean he was over the second district of the city.

11:17.t: Mica: the KJV spells it Micha.

11:23.t: "A fixed provision": the KJV's "a certain portion", a daily allowance.

11:24.t: "The king's agent": the KJV's "at the king's hand", the Jews' representative at the Persian court.

11:25.t: Kiriath-arba: the KJV spells it Kirjath-arba; it is Hebron. Beersheba: the KJV spells it Beer-sheba.

12:1.t: Shecaniah, Ginnethoi, Mijamin: the KJV spells them Shechaniah, Ginnetho, Miamin.

12:9.t: "Shifts of service", "one group answering the other": the KJV's "watches" and "ward over against ward"; the singers stood in two groups that answered each other.

12:24.t: "Shifts of service", "one group answering the other": the KJV's "watches" and "ward over against ward"; the singers stood in two groups that answered each other.

12:10.t: This list of high priests reaches to Jaddua, a generation or two after Nehemiah.

12:22.t: This list of high priests reaches to Jaddua, a generation or two after Nehemiah.

12:14.t: Melicu: as in the KJV; probably the same name as Malluch (verse 2).

12:17.t: "Of Miniamin": the name of the head of that family is missing in the Hebrew.

12:21.t: Nethanel: the KJV spells it Nethaneel. 12:36 Azarel: the KJV spells it Azarael.

12:36.t: Nethanel: the KJV spells it Nethaneel. 12:36 Azarel: the KJV spells it Azarael.

12:25.t: "Thresholds of the gates": as in the KJV. The Hebrew word may mean the storehouses at the gates.

12:27.t: "Harps and lyres": the KJV's "psalteries" and "harps", stringed instruments.

12:28.t: "Netophathites": the KJV's "Netophathi", the people of Netophah near Bethlehem.

12:31.t: "Choirs": the KJV's "companies of them that gave thanks". The two choirs went around the wall in opposite directions and met at the temple.

12:38.t: "Choirs": the KJV's "companies of them that gave thanks". The two choirs went around the wall in opposite directions and met at the temple.

12:40.t: "Choirs": the KJV's "companies of them that gave thanks". The two choirs went around the wall in opposite directions and met at the temple.

12:39.t: "Tower of the Hundred": the KJV's "tower of Meah"; meah is the Hebrew word for "hundred" (see 3:1). "Gate of the Guard": the KJV's "prison gate".

12:45.t: "The charge of their God": the KJV's "the ward of their God", their assigned duties.

13:3.t: "Those of mixed descent": the KJV's "the mixed multitude", meaning those of foreign descent.

13:4.t: "Closely connected": the KJV's "allied", probably by marriage (compare 13:28).

13:6.t: The thirty-second year of Artaxerxes was 433 BC (compare 5:14). How long Nehemiah stayed away is not said. Artaxerxes is called "king of Babylon" because Babylon was part of his empire.

13:24.t: "The language of Judah": the KJV's "the Jews' language", that is, Hebrew.

13:26.t: "Foreign women": the KJV's "outlandish women", in the old sense of women from other lands (1 Kings 11:1-8).

13:28.t: A grandson of the high priest had married into the family of Sanballat, Nehemiah's chief enemy.

9:32.t: "Covenant and steadfast love" (Hebrew berit and hesed): the KJV's "covenant and mercy". hesed is loyal, committed love that keeps its promises, especially within a covenant; no single English word covers it, and the KJV uses "mercy", "kindness" and "lovingkindness" (see Genesis 24:27 and Ezra 3:11). berit, "covenant", is a binding agreement that sets up a relationship with promises and obligations on both sides. Together the words mean that God keeps His promises out of loyal love, not only out of duty.

5:19.t: "Remember me" (Hebrew zakar): to remember in Hebrew is more than to recall; it means to act on behalf of someone, to keep a person in mind for good (Genesis 8:1, "God remembered Noah"). Nehemiah's "remember me for good" asks God to act, not merely to keep a record.

13:14.t: "Remember me" (Hebrew zakar): to remember in Hebrew is more than to recall; it means to act on behalf of someone, to keep a person in mind for good (Genesis 8:1, "God remembered Noah"). Nehemiah's "remember me for good" asks God to act, not merely to keep a record.

13:22.t: "Remember me" (Hebrew zakar): to remember in Hebrew is more than to recall; it means to act on behalf of someone, to keep a person in mind for good (Genesis 8:1, "God remembered Noah"). Nehemiah's "remember me for good" asks God to act, not merely to keep a record.

13:31.t: "Remember me" (Hebrew zakar): to remember in Hebrew is more than to recall; it means to act on behalf of someone, to keep a person in mind for good (Genesis 8:1, "God remembered Noah"). Nehemiah's "remember me for good" asks God to act, not merely to keep a record.

13:2.t: "Turned the curse into a blessing" (Hebrew qelalah and berakah): a summary of Numbers 22-24. A blessing in Hebrew thought is God's gift of life and good; a curse is its removal. The point is that no hired word can overrule what God intends for His people.
